post.title: Why Your Best Friend Is Probably Your Neighbour #shorts
post.description: Met your best friend by chance? Tell me in the comments. Send this to the friend who sat next to you. Lila's new work best friend is Mae, from the next desk. In 1950, Leon Festinger, Stanley Schachter and Kurt Back mapped friendships among married students in MIT's Westgate housing ('Social Pressures in Informal Groups'). Friendships formed most between next-door neighbours, and residents living by the stairways made more friends on other floors. Psychologists call it the proximity (propinquity) effect: we come to like the people we keep bumping into. Chance picks who you meet. You pick who stays. #psychology #shorts #friendship #proximityeffect #overthinking
